_comment: One developer, one Claude Code session. The agent may publish (you review the diff anyway) but may not deploy, destroy, or touch a database. Copy to .indenture/policy.json and loosen it where it annoys you — every refusal lands in the journal with the actors and the kind, so you always know which rule is missing.

rules._: Refusals first — the first matching rule decides, so anything permissive above these would win silently.
rules.reason: this destroys data and cannot be undone. Show me the command and let me run it myself.
deploying is irreversible and I have not reviewed this yet. Tell me what you would deploy and why, and I will run it.
no direct database access. Write a migration or a script I can read first.
publishing a package is effectively irreversible — it cannot be unpublished after 72 hours. Tell me the version and what changed, and I will run it.

rules._: git push is fine: nothing reaches anyone without a review, and a revert undoes it. Blocking it would make this unusable.
You are the operator. Nothing stops you.
